summary:
I'm Divyanshu, an applied AI engineer based in Exeter. I build software that helps people work through messy information and everyday tasks: finding an answer across documents, preparing a job application, or running a shop from a chat.

That takes different forms in my projects. DocChat brings PDFs, YouTube transcripts and web pages into one conversation, with citations and checks against the source material. JobFit connects job discovery, fit analysis and tailored application documents. SuperOps turns Telegram messages into inventory updates, bills and customer credit records for a kirana store. JARVIS brings voice, memory and permission-controlled tools to the Mac.

My foundation is three years of software engineering at Mphasis, working on banking and visa-processing systems, followed by an MSc in Statistical Data Science at Exeter. For my dissertation, I built EPC: a pipeline analysing 1.8 million housing energy records in South West England, combining policy analysis with predictive modelling. That mix of application development and statistical thinking shapes how I build AI today.

aboutCards.title: The details behind the demo
aboutCards.text: I spend time on what happens after a model responds: checking its output, saving progress, recovering from failures and deciding which actions need permission. In SuperOps, the model chooses tools; code handles the money and stock calculations.

aboutCards.title: Making changes measurable
aboutCards.text: I built PromptOps to compare prompt versions, inspect failures and catch regressions. In DocChat, I also work on retrieval evaluation and inference benchmarks, looking at answer quality, latency and cost together.

aboutCards.title: Away from the keyboard
aboutCards.text: Outside engineering, I read, play guitar and go to the gym. I also work part time as a barista at Starbucks, with badminton and table tennis now and then.

Engineered a performance-optimised document processing pipeline, resolving a critical bottleneck and contributing to €12k+ additional revenue.

projects.name: JobFit
projects.summary: Six-agent pipeline that parses a CV and a job spec, scores the match and writes a tailored resume and cover letter. Typed contracts between agents, parallel stages, and per-agent model tiering that cut inference cost by 73%. Deployed on AWS ECS Fargate with CI/CD and monitoring.

projects.name: JARVIS
projects.summary: Voice-first macOS assistant with a three-tier model router (local Ollama, Groq, Claude) that escalates only when a cheaper model fails. About 20 tools behind one safety-gated dispatch layer, three-layer memory, per-request tracing and 69 tests.

projects.name: DocChat
projects.summary: Agentic RAG pipeline with planner, retriever, synthesizer and critic stages. The critic checks each answer against retrieved context before it surfaces. Cross-encoder reranking improved MRR by 28% and Hit@1 by 50%. Exposed as an MCP server.

projects.name: PromptOps
projects.summary: Prompt-as-code evaluation platform with MLflow tracking and LLM-as-judge scoring across OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama. Took a golden test set from 40% to 100% pass rate by iterating on measured results, and cut completion tokens by 29%.
